ancestry_summary.statement_nl: Let $n$ be an integer greater than 1. For which real numbers $x$ is \\[\\lfloor nx \\rfloor - \\sum_{k=1}^{n} \\frac{\\lfloor kx \\rfloor}{k}\\] maximal, and what is the maximal value that this expression can take?

payload.proof_nl: Because j/n <= x < (j+1)/n and n is positive, multiplying the inequality by n preserves the order and gives j <= nx < j+1. Now set t = nx - j. Subtracting j from the displayed inequality yields 0 <= t < 1. Also nx = j + t, so dividing by n gives x = (j+t)/n. The affine reconstruction map on the cell [j/n,(j+1)/n) is exactly T_{n,j}(u) = (j+u)/n, hence x = T_{n,j}(t).
